claim_text: The same perturbation produced ERK activation; lapatinib, trastuzumab, or MEK inhibitors suppressed this ERK rebound and improved proliferation, apoptosis, and xenograft growth endpoints compared with PI3K-pathway inhibition alone `pmid-21278786`.
evidence_summary: In HER2-overexpressing breast cancer models, BEZ235/PI3K-pathway blockade induced ERK phosphorylation; lapatinib, trastuzumab, and MEK inhibitors prevented ERK activation, improved antiproliferative/proapoptotic effects, and enhanced BT474-Tr xenograft tumor growth inhibition.
reviewer_notes: Uses preclinical HER2-positive models and older PI3K/mTOR inhibitors.

claim_text: A genetic in vivo model reinforced that this feedback can matter after an initial response: Her2 plus PIK3CA H1047R mammary tumors regressed after mutant PIK3CA deinduction, but recurrent tumors restored Her2/Her3 and MAPK signaling, and lapatinib plus MEK162 produced sustained regression in recurrent transplants `pmid-26640141`.
evidence_summary: NIC+PIK3CAH1047R tumors regressed after doxycycline withdrawal/inactivation of mutant PIK3CA, but all resumed growth; recurrent tumors showed restored Her2/Her3 and increased p42/p44 MAPK, and lapatinib plus MEK162 produced sustained regression in recurrent transplants.
reviewer_notes: Genetic deinduction is not identical to pharmacologic PI3K-alpha inhibition.

claim_text: In HER2-positive PTEN-deficient breast tumor models, p110-alpha was described as a major effector downstream of RTKs, and combined Her2, p110-alpha, and p110-beta inhibition most strongly reduced AKT activation and minimized tumor growth `pmid-26500061`.
evidence_summary: HER2-positive PTEN-deficient cell and xenograft models showed p110-alpha as the primary mediator of RTK/HER2-driven PI3K-AKT signaling; lapatinib plus BYL719 reduced signaling and growth, and combined HER2, p110-alpha, and p110-beta inhibition maximally abrogated AKT activation and minimized tumor growth.
reviewer_notes: Addresses resistance to HER2-targeted therapy more directly than resistance to PI3K-alpha inhibitors.

claim_text: Other HER2-positive preclinical studies found that adding PI3K inhibitors, including alpelisib or inavolisib, could circumvent trastuzumab resistance in PIK3CA-mutant or PTEN-deficient cell models, with increased apoptosis and in vivo synergy reported, although the clinical translatability and toxicity of such combinations remain unsettled `pmid-35968355`.
evidence_summary: HER2-positive trastuzumab-resistant HCC1954, UACC893, and HCC1569 models with PIK3CA mutation and/or PTEN deficiency responded to alpelisib or GDC-0077 plus trastuzumab with pathway suppression, increased apoptosis, in vitro synergy, and alpelisib-plus-trastuzumab xenograft tumor reduction; discussion notes human studies and toxicity remain unresolved.
reviewer_notes: The paper names GDC-0077 rather than consistently using the later generic name inavolisib, but the cited evidence otherwise supports the statement.

claim_text: This trial supports feasibility of HER2-HER3-PI3K cotargeting, but it was primarily a safety and dose-finding study and emphasizes overlapping toxicity rather than definitive resistance reversal `pmid-33947692`.
evidence_summary: The phase I study tested alpelisib plus trastuzumab plus LJM716 in PIK3CA-mutant HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer to establish MTD; grade 3 or higher diarrhea and other toxicities were common, the conclusion says gastrointestinal toxicity limited the combination, and efficacy was secondary/preliminary.
reviewer_notes: Clinical activity data were limited and not designed to prove resistance reversal.

claim_text: In luminal and triple-negative breast cancer models, NRG1, EGF, and FGF10 protected cells from alpelisib and reactivated AKT, S6, 4E-BP1, and ERK; SHP2 overexpression conferred resistance, while SHP2 inhibition, knockout, or phosphatase-dead reconstitution experiments showed that SHP2 was needed for RTK-mediated resistance and that PI3K plus SHP2 inhibition suppressed organoid and xenograft growth `pmid-35365185`.
evidence_summary: BYL719-treated luminal/TNBC cells were protected by RTK ligands including NRG1, EGF, and FGF10 with rebound AKT/S6/4E-BP1/ERK signaling; SHP2 overexpression induced resistance, SHP099/knockout and phosphatase-dead reconstitution experiments showed SHP2 dependence, and BYL719/SHP099 suppressed patient-derived organoids and HCC1806 xenografts.

claim_text: In squamous carcinoma models, acquired alpelisib resistance involved AXL overexpression, AXL-EGFR interaction, and downstream PLC-gamma-PKC signaling that maintained mTOR despite PI3K-AKT inhibition; resistance was reversed by combining PI3K-alpha inhibition with EGFR, AXL, or PKC blockade `pmid-25873175`.
evidence_summary: Head and neck/esophageal SCC models resistant to BYL719 overexpressed AXL; AXL interacted with EGFR and activated PLC-gamma/PKC, sustaining mTOR despite PI3K/AKT inhibition, and combined PI3K-alpha inhibition with EGFR, AXL, or PKC inhibitors reversed resistance.
reviewer_notes: Different lineage from breast cancer, though claim states squamous carcinoma.

claim_text: EGFR ligand signaling can also drive acquired PI3K inhibitor resistance outside breast cancer, as SW48 colorectal models selected in pictilisib secreted amphiregulin, maintained EGFR-MAPK signaling, and gained sensitivity to EGFR or MAPK cotargeting `pmid-25053989`.
evidence_summary: SW48/SW48 H1047R colorectal models selected in GDC-0941 secreted amphiregulin, used EGFR-MAPK signaling to grow under PI3K inhibition, and were resensitized by EGFR inhibitors or MEK/ERK cotargeting, including xenograft settings.
reviewer_notes: Outside breast cancer and uses pictilisib/GDC-0941.

claim_text: Likewise, IGF1R upregulation maintained AKT-mTOR signaling and conferred acquired resistance to GDC0032 or alpelisib in PIK3CA-driven ovarian cancer, with IGF1R inhibition restoring sensitivity `pmid-30237504`.
evidence_summary: PIK3CA-driven ovarian cancer resistant models upregulated IGF1R, which reactivated/maintained AKT-mTOR signaling under GDC0032 and BYL719; IGF1R inhibition with AEW541 enhanced sensitivity to both drugs in vitro and in vivo.
